hooks.command: cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""' | tr '\n' ';'); printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -Eq '(^|[;&|(])[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?docker([[:space:]]|$)' && { printf "Blocked: this session runs INSIDE the dev container - there is no docker CLI and never will be. Reach services over the compose network by name (proxy:8080, api:8000, db:5432), or run the tool directly.\n" >&2; exit 2; }; exit 0

cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""')
# POSIX `case`, never `[[ ]]`: hook commands run under /bin/sh, which is dash
# here. dash has no `[[`, so a bash-syntax test errors, the condition reads as
# false, and the hook silently exits 0 - blocking nothing, forever.
case "$cmd" in
  *"npm test"*|*"ng test"*|*pytest*)
    case "$cmd" in
      *"|"*)
        printf "Blocked: piping a test run truncates the output at the terminal, which is what leads to running the suite a second time to find what was cut off. Capture all of it and report the exit code:\n  npm test > /tmp/test.log 2>&1; echo exit=\$?\nRead /tmp/test.log ONLY when that exit is non-zero. On a pass the exit code is the whole answer and reading the log is wasted.\n" >&2
        exit 2 ;;
    esac ;;
esac
exit 0

root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
cd "$root" || exit 0
PC=$(command -v pre-commit) || { printf "pre-commit not found on PATH\n" >&2; exit 1; }
list=$( { git diff --name-only HEAD; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } | sort -u )
[ -n "$list" ] || exit 0
oldIFS=$IFS
IFS="
"
set --
for f in $list; do
  set -- "$@" "$f"
done
IFS=$oldIFS
idx=$(mktemp) || exit 0
cp "$(git rev-parse --git-path index)" "$idx" || exit 0
export GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx"
"$PC" run --files "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { out=$("$PC" run --files "$@" 2>&1) || { rm -f "$idx"; printf "%s\n" "$out" >&2; exit 2; }; }
rm -f "$idx"
